text:
Aisha: quick smoke: noticed ~9-12% token/sec drop after we flipped kernel-chooser to prefer fused-paged for bfloat16 when using the interleaved KV layout. posting quick numbers and plan. :eyes:

Marc: can you paste the perf numbers and exact run command?

Aisha: run on s2.large-gpu (A100), model=redwood-3b, batch=4, seq=32, dtype=bfloat16
```
baseline (separate-kv + old kernel): 1250 tok/s
new (interleaved + fused-paged preference): 1125 tok/s
allocs show extra memcpy in kv copy path (~1.8x)
```

perf-bot: flamegraph -> http://perf.internal/fg/1987654321 (will attach trace)

Olga: interesting. did you try fp16? bfloat path sometimes triggers alignment/fallbacks on the fused kernels.

Aisha: yes fp16 is fine: 1230 tok/s. regression is specific to bfloat16 + interleaved.

Diego: my gut: stride/padding difference. interleaved layout uses 128-byte per-key alignment in our allocator; bfloat16 doubling element width might cause non-coalesced loads for the fused-paged kernel.

Lin: quick triage checklist: run nsys to confirm memcpy vs kernel time, toggle KV_ALIGN_BYTES env, and run microbench for copy vs kernel. Also try batch sweep (1,2,4,8) — heuristics might pick wrong kernel for small batches.

Marc: noted. for batching heuristics: we saw earlier that fused-paged wins at batch>=8 for these seqs; for batch 2-4 flash-fused or flash-packed is usually better. We should update kernel-selector rule to consider (dtype, layout, batch, seq).

Aisha: repro script + logs attached. I will run nsys and post the trace. plan: 1) reproduce with nsys 2) test KV_ALIGN_BYTES=256 and 64 3) microbench memcpy vs kernel with interleaved/separate 4) adjust selector and add guard to prefer non-fused for bfloat16+interleaved small-batch until fixed.

Olga: sgtm. also add a regression test in CI that runs small-seq bfloat interleaved perf smoke so we catch this early.

perf-bot: PERF-3421 created: "bfloat16 perf regression when fused-paged chosen on interleaved KV"

Aisha: will attach nsys link when done and ping here. thanks folks. :thumbsup:
